$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. Every node key carries written_by, naming the node that wrote it: that is the ONLY record of authorship this file has, and without it 'never rewrite another node's key' is unverifiable - an orchestrator hand-writing all six keys is indistinguishable from six nodes doing their jobs. verify-state.py --audit checks it. This file is the edge: it is how context crosses between agents that cannot see each other.

plan.intent: Process-tree kill on Linux (cfg(unix) group, cfg(target_os=linux) PDEATHSIG). Spawn: cmd.process_group(0) (std CommandExt, no setsid) so claude leads a new group whose pgid == its pid; there is no assign-after-spawn race as on Windows. A new cfg(unix) module (e.g. core/src/session/process/group.rs) implements the same terminate()/active() surface the Windows Job has: terminate() = libc::kill(-pgid, SIGKILL); active() = 1 while kill(-pgid, 0) succeeds or returns EPERM, 0 on ESRCH. attach_job returns Some on unix, so ProcessHandle::kill, wait_exit and the reader keep their existing job-shaped code paths (kill takes no child lock, reader blocks in wait(), wait_exit waits for the group to empty). Pid-reuse guard: after reaping the leader, the reader thread keeps probing the group with capped backoff (<= 1 s) until ESRCH and then sets a gone flag; terminate() is a no-op once gone, so a Drop hours later can never signal a recycled pgid. PDEATHSIG: on Linux only, every spawn_program call hands its Command to one process-lifetime spawner thread (OnceLock'd mpsc channel; Command is Send) which calls spawn() and returns the Child; a pre_exec hook (unsafe, async-signal-safe calls only) does prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGKILL) and then _exit(1)s if getppid() differs from the ppid captured before fork. This answers the scout's plan-killer: the pump/retry/free_slot threads that call spawn are short-lived, but the thread that actually forks never exits before the process does. Windows: job.rs untouched, CREATE_NO_WINDOW path untouched, no spawner thread (cfg linux only). The NotFound error string stays byte-identical on Windows; off Windows it names claude, not claude.exe. The pipe comment at process.rs:190-193 is made OS-neutral (on unix the child's fd 0/1 are inherited by grandchildren too). Tests (cfg(unix) unless named linux_), all through the real spawn_program: unix_kill_reaches_the_grandchild (sh -c 'sleep 60 & echo $!; wait', read the grandchild pid from Output::Line, kill(), wait_exit(5 s) == true, grandchild absent or state Z in /proc/<pid>/stat); unix_wait_exit_waits_for_the_group (sh -c 'sleep 1 >/dev/null </dev/null 2>&1 & echo $!' exits at once; wait_exit returns true only after the grandchild is gone, elapsed >= 800 ms); unix_group_is_gone_after_it_empties (gone flag set, terminate is then a no-op); linux_a_child_outlives_the_thread_that_spawned_it (spawn from a std::thread, join it, then wait_exit(500 ms) == false: the regression test for the plan-killer); linux_pdeathsig_kills_the_child_when_the_host_dies (the test re-executes its own test binary with an env var to run an #[ignore]d helper that spawns sh -c 'echo $$; exec sleep 60' through spawn_program, prints the pid and calls std::process::abort(); the outer test asserts that pid is absent or Z within 5 s, then kills any leftovers). The helper is a no-op without its env var.

architect.rationale: SINGLE-LOOP. One app, one branch, and every Linux claim in s1-s3 is proven by the same CI run that s4 creates, so the slices are not independently checkable: their Linux done_when all consume the s4 workflow on one pushed branch. A diamond would need three branches and three pushes for one evidence source. The file sets are disjoint (s1 process.rs/group.rs/core Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock; s2 the test modules of git.rs and session/mod.rs; s3 paths.rs/lib.rs; s4 test.yml; s5 ROADMAP.md/CLAUDE.md), which keeps review per slice clean, but disjoint files without independent done_when is a sequence, not a diamond. BUILDER ORDER on branch h1-linux-core cut from main @ 5efc224: record the Windows baseline (cargo test --workspace --locked counts, and the junction count from -- --list) before any edit; s3, s2, s1 with Windows tests green locally (plus the linux cargo check if G6); s4; then stop for the push gate (G7); iterate on CI; s5 last with the real counts. Commits authored by the configured owner identity (njcurtis3), no Claude trailers. TREE-KILL DESIGN (answers the plan-killer): hybrid. The process group is the primary mechanism for every graceful path (stop, stop_and_wait, pause_and_wait, shutdown, Drop) and mirrors the terminate/active surface of the Windows Job, so the kill/wait/reap logic in process.rs is reused rather than forked by OS. PDEATHSIG is crash insurance for the direct child only, and it is set from one process-lifetime spawner thread because prctl binds to the forking thread and every current spawn site (mod.rs:990-995 pump_in_background, 910-913 retry_pending_in_background, 1262-1265 free_slot) is a one-shot thread; setting it there would SIGKILL claude when the pump thread returned. Rejected: PDEATHSIG from the existing call sites (the plan-killer); group-only (offered as G1 option b: simpler, no spawner thread, but claude survives an app crash on Linux); setsid instead of setpgid (a new session buys nothing here, and std process_group(0) needs no unsafe). CRASH BEHAVIOUR: Windows - the kernel closes the job handle when the app dies and KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE kills claude and every descendant that did not break away. Linux after H1 - the spawner thread dies with the process and PDEATHSIG SIGKILLs claude; the descendants of claude are NOT signalled, are reparented, and run on in the orphaned group until they exit (a writer gets SIGPIPE on the dead stdout; a quiet one such as sleep or a dev server survives). SIGTERM to the desktop on Linux (logout) behaves like a crash because shutdown() does not run. Parity is NOT required for H1: graceful paths reach parity via killpg, and crash parity is deferred to H2, where orchestrad runs under systemd and KillMode=control-group (the default) kills the whole cgroup on stop or crash. The Linux desktop crash gap stays open and is recorded in ROADMAP (s5); a later fix would be a systemd-run --user --scope per session or a supervisor, not H1. PID REUSE: a Windows job handle cannot be recycled; a pgid can, once the group empties. The reader keeps probing until ESRCH and latches gone, bounding the window to one probe interval (<= 1 s), which pid wrap-around cannot cross. A grandchild that calls setsid escapes the group (as a breakaway child escapes a job); documented, not handled. DEPENDENCIES: process_group(0) is std. killpg and prctl are not, so libc is required under either G1 option. libc 0.2.190 is already in Cargo.lock as a transitive package, so a cfg(unix) target dependency libc = 0.2 adds no crate, but it is a new direct dependency of orchestra-core and goes to the gate (G2). Shelling out to /bin/kill was rejected (a process per kill, PATH-dependent). RISK TAGS: s1 high - new unsafe (pre_exec, kill) outside job.rs, pid-reuse logic no test can fully see, Linux-only code that cannot be compiled on this machine without G6, and Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock. s2 low - test-module-only change, no production line, no sensitive data, no file another slice touches; the CI log naming each test plus helpers that assert is_symlink is sufficient evidence. s3 low - pure function, env injected, no caller, no shared file, no data moved. s4 high - it is the only evidence source for every Linux claim (a job that silently skips or runs on the wrong arch makes the s1-s3 done_when vacuous), and it is a public-repo workflow where permissions and action pinning are security-relevant and only partly grep-checkable. s5 low - prose in two files no other slice touches, partly human-read. CI ITERATION: at most 4 pushes of h1-linux-core in total (the first plus 3 fix cycles); each cycle is push, gh run watch / gh run view --log-failed, fix, commit. Escalate to the orchestrator on the 4th red run, or at once when a failure points at the design rather than a typo: the PDEATHSIG or grandchild test failing because of a runner subreaper or /proc behaviour; the arm64 runner unavailable or queued over 15 min (never swap runners silently); a pre-existing core test failing on Linux for a real platform reason (a scope question, not a fix-to-green). Never force-push, never weaken or delete a test to get green, never add continue-on-error. NATIVE RULES: ui is native-desktop + native-mobile, but no slice touches tauri.conf.json, capabilities, app.json, eas.json or a native module, so there is no runtimeVersion or new-build consequence. The Windows rule holds: every local done_when runs on Windows; every Linux done_when is a named CI job on ubuntu-24.04 / ubuntu-24.04-arm read with gh. No cross-app reads.

s1.$comment: RE-REVIEWS NEST, and this is the rule every reader follows. The TOP LEVEL of reviews.<slice> IS attempt 1. A re-review writes attempt_2, then attempt_3, and so on, each with the same fields as the top level. Every attempt SURVIVES PERMANENTLY - history is never overwritten, flattened, or migrated up. The LATEST attempt supplies the verdict: that is what close-run.py, brief.py and verify-state.py resolve through, and what fleetview's finalVerdict() has always shown. `ever_rejected` - did ANY attempt REJECT - is DISPLAY ONLY, forever, so a rejection stays visible after it is fixed; it must never gate anything, or the fleet stops being able to loop. NO NODE MAY REWRITE AN EARLIER ATTEMPT: a second reviewer writes its own attempt_N and leaves the ones before it alone, top-level verdict included - relocating that verdict would destroy the history the board keeps and leave a key stamped written_by:reviewer with someone else as its real author. The KEY INDEX numbers an attempt, not the `attempt` field inside it; the field is display. An EMPTY attempt_N is not a re-review, it is a key nobody wrote - write the whole attempt or none of it. The walk STOPS AT THE FIRST GAP, so an attempt_3 with no attempt_2 is ignored and the earlier verdict stands: A GAP IS MALFORMED AND NO NODE MAY LEAVE ONE. Write the next UNUSED N and never skip - a mis-numbered re-review is not reported anywhere, it is simply unread, and a REJECT nobody reads is a REJECT nobody acts on. The cap is attempt_9, matching fleetview's `for (i = 2; i < 10; i++)` exactly so the two readers cannot disagree; attempt_10 and beyond is reported loudly and resolved by nobody.

Re-ran myself at 3df974a: cargo test --workspace --locked on Windows (shell 10, core 185, wire_fixtures 4, all 0 failed); git diff --quiet main -- job.rs desktop/ exit 0; Cargo.lock delta is exactly '+ "libc",'; cargo check -p orchestra-core --tests --locked --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu exit 0, no warnings. Pulled the ubuntu x86_64 and aarch64 core job logs for both green runs: all 5 s1 tests print '... ok' in each (uname confirms arch), 185 passed 1 ignored. Re-derived by hand: process_group(0) runs in the child before exec and spawn() returns only after exec, so no group race; kill(-pgid,0) with EPERM=alive/else=gone is right and an unreaped zombie leader pins the pgid; the gone latch leaves only a <=1 s pid-wrap window. The spawner thread can never exit (static Sender), and if it panicked every later spawn errors loudly via a closed channel, never hangs. pre_exec only does prctl/getppid/_exit/errno, no allocation. Notes: a no-reaper PID-1 container never empties the group; the gone test cannot observe terminate as a no-op.

findings.issue: active() counts zombies (correct per kernel semantics). Where nothing reaps orphans - orchestra running as PID 1 in a container without tini/--init, relevant to the headless H track - SIGKILLed grandchildren reparent to orchestra and stay Z forever: wait_exit always returns false after kill() and the reader thread probes at 1 s forever per session. Not reachable on a desktop or a systemd host. Worth a line in H2/H3 (run under an init, or set PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER and reap).

Residual TOCTOU: between the group emptying and the reader's next probe (<=1 s, capped backoff) gone is still false, so a terminate() in that window does kill(-pgid). Hitting an unrelated process needs the pid to be reallocated and made a group leader within that second, i.e. a full pid_max wrap. Accepted risk, not a blocker; the plan's design.

unix_group_is_gone_after_it_empties asserts is_gone() and active()==0, but active()==0 is tautological once gone is latched, and terminate() being a no-op is not observed (comment says so). The latch is covered by reading the code, not by the test.

spawner::spawn calls std::thread::spawn inside OnceLock::get_or_init; if thread creation fails it panics in the caller (pump/retry thread) instead of returning Err like cmd.spawn() did. OnceLock retries on the next call, so it does not wedge. Rare (resource exhaustion).

On Unix the reader thread now outlives Exit while in-group descendants live, holding the sink (Arc to the session manager) until the group empties or the handle is dropped (Drop kills the group). Bounded and matches the job semantics; mentioned so H2 is not surprised by lingering threads.

Descendants that setsid() (e.g. node child_process with detached:true) leave the group and are neither killed nor waited for, and PDEATHSIG covers claude only. Documented in the module doc and deferred by G3 to H2; recorded so it is not lost.
